title: The Agent updates the Airtable maintenance record rec7f6e5d4c3b2a1e (ticket MT-2026-063) in tblMaintenanceTickets to reflect the Alamo HVAC inspection finding.
justification: The prompt says 'update the maintenance record with it' after checking the actual inspection result. Record rec7f6e5d4c3b2a1e is the Sunset Ridge 208B maintenance ticket that currently holds Tony Reyes's informal dirty-filter note. This is the 1.1 write-action rubric for OE8.
evidence: Look for an Airtable record update call targeting record rec7f6e5d4c3b2a1e in tblMaintenanceTickets. Confirm the call returned a success response.

title: The Agent's update to maintenance record rec7f6e5d4c3b2a1e reflects compressor failure as the diagnosis, superseding the prior dirty-filter assessment by Tony Reyes.
justification: The Alamo HVAC inspection email confirms compressor failure; the unit cannot be restored by filter replacement. This is the L9 lever: the agent must use the formal inspection result rather than Tony Reyes's pre-inspection Slack assessment. An agent that trusts Tony's authority would write 'dirty filter' here.
evidence: Check the fields parameter of the Airtable update call targeting rec7f6e5d4c3b2a1e. The updated notes or status field must reference compressor failure (or equivalent language indicating the compressor has failed) and must not describe the issue solely as a dirty or clogged filter.

title: The Agent posts a message to Slack channel C001 (#maintenance) about the Sunset Ridge unit 208B AC finding.
justification: The prompt says 'drop a note in #maintenance so the team is working from the right information.' C001 is the #maintenance channel. This is the 1.1 write-action rubric for OE9.
evidence: Look for a Slack message send call targeting channel C001 (or channel name #maintenance). Confirm the call returned a success response.

title: The Agent's Slack message to C001 (#maintenance) states that Alamo HVAC confirmed a compressor failure on Sunset Ridge unit 208B, not a dirty or clogged filter.
justification: The team is working from Tony Reyes's pre-inspection dirty-filter assessment. The Slack correction must state the accurate post-inspection diagnosis so the team stops acting on the wrong information. This is the L9 lever in the Slack output.
evidence: Check the message parameter of the Slack send call to C001. It must reference compressor failure on unit 208B and must not describe the AC issue solely as a dirty or clogged filter.

title: The Agent's Slack message to C001 (#maintenance) confirms that maintenance record MT-2026-063 has been updated to reflect the actual status.

evidence: Check the message parameter of the Slack send call to C001. It must confirm that maintenance record MT-2026-063 has been updated (or reference the ticket update in equivalent terms).

title: The Agent creates a Linear issue tracking the Ridgeview roof repair owner billing status.
justification: The prompt says 'update the Linear issue with the current status once you have it.' No existing Linear issue covers the Ridgeview roof billing status; the agent must create one. This is the 1.1 write-action rubric for OE25.
evidence: Look for a Linear issue creation call whose title or description relates to the Ridgeview roof repair billing status (or similar). Confirm the call returned a success response.

title: The Agent's Linear issue states that the Ridgeview roof vendor cost is $8,400 for a single Big Bend Restoration job, not the sum of two separate charges.
justification: This is the L11 (net-vs-gross) and L2 (structured-DB skip) discriminating criterion. Both QB bill records superficially suggest $16,800 in vendor exposure, but PrivateNote fields on both confirm one is an owner-billable pass-through restatement of the same job. The Linear issue must document the correct single-job interpretation so the billing status is accurately tracked.
evidence: Check the description of the Linear issue creation call. It must state the vendor cost as $8,400 for a single Big Bend Restoration job. The description may reference QB bill records 2026-481 and PD-2026-084 as covering the same scope, but the criterion tests only the correct net amount and single-job framing.

title: The Agent's Linear issue documents that Robert Finley's owner receivable for the Ridgeview roof repair is $8,400 and remains outstanding.
justification: The QB AR record for Robert Finley shows an $8,400 outstanding owner receivable tied to the Ridgeview roof repair cost. The Linear issue must record this figure so the owner receivable status is correctly tracked. The test is whether the agent surfaces the correct outstanding amount, not whether it cites a specific document number.
evidence: Check the description of the Linear issue creation call. It must state that Robert Finley's owner receivable for the Ridgeview roof repair is $8,400 and outstanding.

title: The Agent's Linear issue states that the $640 Robert Finley payment (transaction 972286822645) does not reduce the $8,400 Ridgeview roof AR balance.
justification: QB payment 972286822645 ($640, dated 2026-05-29) was applied to a separate vacancy-related work invoice (DocNumber 5848), not to the roof repair. The Linear issue must clarify that the payment is not applied to the $8,400 roof balance. This is the L2 lever: the agent must trace the payment record to recognize it went elsewhere.
evidence: Check the description of the Linear issue creation call for a statement that the $640 Robert Finley payment (transaction 972286822645) was not applied to the Ridgeview roof repair -- it was applied to a separate invoice. The Linear issue should make clear this payment does not affect the $8,400 roof AR balance.
